newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm in line with Bunds, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm in line with Bunds, trade thin.

text.p: Irish bond prices were marked up in line with Germany on Friday, with the 10-year bond slightly outperforming the Bund, but trade was at a minimum, dealers said.

"The curve has shifted down across Europe today but there's nothing in the way of news and we've seen very little international or domestic interest," a dealer said. "I think traders have probably closed off the week at this stage and are looking ahead."
By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 18 pence at 102.13 to yield 5.92 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was up 33 pence at 109.88 to yield 6.53 percent.
Yields against German Bunds were broadly unchanged from the close at 154 basis points over in the five-year bond, and 90 over in the 10-year.
With the week ahead relatively quiet data-wise, German inflation in the form of import and export prices will most likely provide the main market-focus, dealers said.
German inflation is expected to tick up to 1.6 percent from 1.5 percent, one dealer said.
U.S. consumer confidence data on Tuesday could set the tone for the week.
Also expected are U.S. durable orders and revisions to U.S. GDP.
Dealers said they did not anticipate any impact from the G7 financial summit which began in Denver today.
Analysts said however that trade friction between Japan and the United States was threatening to dominate the summit and shake up the dollar/yen exchange rate.
Unless G7 leaders, meeting this weekend in Denver, show concern about a rising Japanese trade surplus, yen bulls will feel free to charge again, economists said on Friday.
This could have a ripple-effect for bond buyers, who in the past used Japan's paltry interest rates to finance their bond purchases, they added.
